A Pushdown Automaton (PDA) is another type of theoretical machine used in automata theory. It is more powerful than a DFA because it has an additional feature: a stack. The stack allows the PDA to handle a wider range of languages, specifically context-free languages.

response:
In theoretical computer science, a language is said to be decidable if there is a Turing machine that accepts every string in the language and rejects every string not in the language. 

If a language contains finitely many strings, then it is indeed decidable. This is because we can construct a Turing machine that simply stores all the strings in the language. When given a string as input, the Turing machine can simply check if the string is in its stored list. If it is, the machine accepts; if it isn't, the machine rejects. This process will always terminate, so the language is decidable.
